claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr is considered as a single-phase bcc refractory high-entropy alloy in the proposed operating regime.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr state is a random solid solution without long-range chemical order.
Controlled annealing at 800-1200 K can induce chemical short-range order in the alloy.
Further thermal treatment can connect SRO clusters into a percolating network.
The alloy remains single-phase bcc across the stated 300-1500 K operating range.
Percolating chemically ordered domains create a continuous pathway through the bcc lattice.
The percolating SRO network creates periodic spatial modulation of the potential-energy surface.
Below the percolation threshold, isolated SRO clusters scatter phonons and reduce thermal conductivity.
Above the percolation threshold, the connected SRO network opens a bandgap-like feature in the phonon density of states.
The proposed phononic bandgap suppresses anharmonic phonon-phonon scattering.
Connected ordered pathways enable coherent phonon transport.
Reduced anharmonic scattering and coherent transport produce a net increase in lattice thermal conductivity above percolation.
Thermal conductivity reaches a minimum at the SRO percolation threshold.
Thermal conductivity increases both below and above the percolation threshold.
The increase above percolation is nonlinear and scales with SRO-network connectivity.
Serial, parallel, and effective-medium models treating SRO as isolated scatterers predict a monotonic decrease in conductivity with increasing SRO.
The critical percolation threshold is approximately 16-20% SRO-cluster volume fraction for a three-dimensional random network.
Phase separation or transformation to an intermetallic compound invalidates the proposed SRO-percolation mechanism.
A suitable potential-energy surface must accurately reproduce SRO energetics and SRO evolution.
PDF analysis can quantify SRO-cluster size and connectivity sufficiently to identify the proposed percolation threshold.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism say that increasing sub-threshold SRO reduces conductivity, whereas the predicted outcome says conductivity increases below the threshold. The latter is also inconsistent with reaching a minimum at the threshold when SRO concentration is the independent variable.
